description: Literature data behind Figure 1 (revision 3): global traffic volumes and selected laboratory and commercial single-core single-mode-fiber transmission capacities. Every value carries its source, locator and verification. Levels follow cards.py: V0 transcribed only (or taken from a secondary source), V1 value, unit and applicability confirmed against the primary source (publisher abstract, open full text or the issuing organization's own page). Checked 2026-11-17.

unit_conventions.occupied_bandwidth: number of channels x channel spacing (sum of channel slots, gaps between bands excluded) unless stated otherwise

cisco_vni_table1.series_label: Global Internet traffic (Cisco VNI, Table 1, 'historical Internet context')

source.citation: Cisco Systems, Cisco Visual Networking Index: Forecast and Trends, 2017-2022, White Paper (Cisco public), San Jose, CA, 2018
source.locator: Table 1 'The Cisco VNI forecast: historical Internet context', p. 5; column heading 'Global internet traffic'; 'Source: Cisco VNI, 2018.'
source.note: Copy read: page footer '(c) 2018 Cisco and/or its affiliates'. The 2017 value (46,600 GB/s) equals Cisco's total IP traffic of the same document (122 EB per month = 46,400 GB/s), although the table heading says Internet traffic (Internet = 13 of 16 GB per capita per month in 2017).

verification.how: Table 1 read in the PDF of the white paper

itu_ff2024.series_label: End-user Internet traffic over fixed and mobile broadband networks (ITU Facts and Figures 2024)

source.citation: International Telecommunication Union, Facts and Figures 2024 - Internet traffic, ITU, Geneva, 2024
source.locator: web page; 'In 2023 mobile broadband traffic ... reached 1 zettabyte'; 'Fixed broadband traffic will reach 6 ZB in 2024, up from 5.1 ZB the previous year'; 2024 mobile 'close to 1.3 ZB' (estimate)

lab_records.citation: H. Onaka, H. Miyata, G. Ishikawa, et al., '1.1 Tb/s WDM transmission over a 150 km 1.3 um zero-dispersion single-mode fiber', Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC 1996), San Jose, CA, postdeadline paper PD19
lab_records.rate_basis: net line rate without FEC (55 x 20 Gb/s)
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: 55 channels x mean spacing; mean spacing = frequency span of 1531.70-1564.07 nm / 54 = 75.0 GHz (computed in the script)
lab_records.spans: 3 x 50 km (in-line EDFAs every 50 km, dispersion-compensating fiber in repeaters and preamplifier)

verification.level: V1 for capacity, distance and fiber (publisher abstract page); V0 for channel count, channel rate, wavelength range and span length (secondary source)
verification.secondary_source: Laser Focus World news report on OFC'96 postdeadline papers (1996): 55 channels at 20 Gb/s, 1531.70-1564.07 nm, 150 km, 50 km amplifier spacing
verification.note: Crossref has no DOI for this postdeadline paper (10.1364/OFC.1996.PD19 returns 404). Confirm the channel plan in the PD19 paper before publication.

lab_records.citation: S. Bigo, Y. Frignac, G. Charlet, et al., '10.2Tbit/s (256x42.7Gbit/s PDM/WDM) transmission over 100km TeraLight fiber with 1.28bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency', OFC 2001, Anaheim, CA, postdeadline paper PD25
lab_records.rate_basis: net payload rate: 256 channels x 42.7 Gb/s line rate = 10.9 Tb/s including FEC overhead; 10.2 Tb/s excludes it (inferred from the title values)
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: capacity / stated SE = 10.2 / 1.28 (computed in the script); channel plan not verified (128 wavelengths x 2 polarizations; trade-press descriptions of the spacing conflict)
lab_records.spans: 100 km (span count not stated in the abstract; presumably one span)
lab_records.fiber: TeraLight non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber (not standard SMF)

verification.how: title and abstract on the publisher page (Optica)

lab_records.citation: D. Qian, M.-F. Huang, E. Ip, et al., '101.7-Tb/s (370x294-Gb/s) PDM-128QAM-OFDM transmission over 3x55-km SSMF using pilot-based phase noise mitigation', OFC/NFOEC 2011, Los Angeles, CA, postdeadline paper PDPB5
lab_records.rate_basis: net rate after FEC overhead: 370 x 294 Gb/s = 108.8 Tb/s raw, 101.7 Tb/s net
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: 370 x 25 GHz (computed in the script); consistent with 101.7 Tb/s / 11 b/s/Hz = 9.25 THz
lab_records.amplifiers: all-Raman (comparison table in Chin. Opt. Lett. 2014, secondary)

verification.how: title and abstract on the publisher page; 25 GHz grid and C+L from the extended version (J. Lightwave Technol. 30(10), 1540-1548, 2012) as summarized by indexes

lab_records.citation: L. Galdino, A. Edwards, W. Yi, et al., 'Optical fibre capacity optimisation via continuous bandwidth amplification and geometric shaping', IEEE Photonics Technol. Lett. 32(17), 1021-1024 (2020)
lab_records.rate_basis: achievable information rate from the measured per-channel GMI with the 4.64 % pilot overhead deducted (AWGN auxiliary channel); not FEC-decoded; called 'net throughput' by the authors
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: stated continuous bandwidth; equals 660 x 25.5 GHz
lab_records.fiber: Corning SMF-28 ULL ultra-low-loss single-mode fiber, 0.16 dB/km at C-band plus 0.4 dB splice/connector loss (ITU-T category not checked)
lab_records.amplifiers: TDFA (1484.86-1519.8 nm), discrete Raman (1520-1529 nm and 1608-1619.67 nm), C- and L-band EDFAs

verification.how: abstract (Semantic Scholar record) and accepted-manuscript full text (UCL Discovery), Sec. I, II and IV

lab_records.citation: B. J. Puttnam, R. S. Luis, Y. Huang, et al., '301 Tb/s E, S, C+L-band transmission over 212 nm bandwidth with E-band bismuth-doped fiber amplifier and gain equalizer', ECOC 2023, Glasgow, pp. 1674-1677
lab_records.rate_basis: 301 Tb/s after LDPC decoding at 50 km; 321 Tb/s GMI-based (NICT release of 29 Jan 2024; J. Lightwave Technol. 42(11), 4006-4012 (2024): '321 Tb/s (301 Tb/s after decoding)')
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: 1097 x 25 GHz = 27.4 THz (computed in the script); the span 1410.8-1623.1 nm is 27.8 THz
lab_records.spans: 1 x 50 km for the record value (single spans up to 150 km and 2 x 100 km also reported)
lab_records.amplifiers: E-band BDFA with E-band gain equalizer, thulium- and erbium-doped amplifiers, backward distributed Raman

verification.how: ECOC abstract (Aston research portal), NICT press release, abstract of the extended JLT version

lab_records.citation: B. J. Puttnam, R. S. Luis, I. Phillips, et al., '402 Tb/s GMI data-rate OESCLU-band transmission', OFC 2024, San Diego, CA, postdeadline paper Th4A.3
lab_records.bandwidth_basis: stated transmission bandwidth; equals 1505 x 25 GHz
lab_records.spans: 50 km (span count not stated in the abstract; presumably one span)

lab_records.amplifiers: six types of doped-fiber amplifier, discrete and distributed Raman

verification.how: publisher abstract (Optica) and NICT press release of 26 Jun 2024 (channel count, wavelength range)

lab_records.citation: R. S. Luis, J. Yang, R. Aparecido, et al., '450 Tb/s GMI, 42.4 THz, OESCL-band transmission over a field-deployed fiber', OFC 2026, Los Angeles, CA, postdeadline paper Th4B.5

lab_records.amplifiers: BDFA (O- and E-band), TDFA (S-band), EDFA (C- and L-band)

commercial_systems.description: state-of-the-art commercial WDM system: 16 channels at 2.5 Gb/s, SE 0.0125 b/s/Hz, up to 40 Gb/s aggregate
commercial_systems.bandwidth_basis: capacity / stated SE = 3.2 THz (16 x 200 GHz)

commercial_systems.description: commercial long-haul system: up to 192 channels at up to 250 Gb/s on a 50 GHz grid, SE 5 b/s/Hz, about 48 Tb/s

excluded.why: forecast made in 2018; reported ITU values for 2023 exist
